ing: optional; use water to skip wine
st: Toss the chicken with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Leave it for 15 minutes.
Cook the onions in a dry heavy pot over medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring often, until soft and sweet without browning.
Add the niter kibbeh, garlic and ginger and cook 3 minutes.
Stir in [[4 tbsp]] berbere and cook 10 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is deep red and thick.
Add the wine, [[1.5 cups]] water and [[1.5 tsp]] salt and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken, cover and cook on low for 45 minutes, turning the pieces once, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Lightly prick the eggs with a fork, add them, and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes so they take on the color.
Taste, adjust the salt, and serve with injera.
Whisk the teff flour with [[3 cups]] water in a large bowl until completely smooth. The batter should be as thin as heavy cream.
Cover loosely and leave at room temperature for at least 10 hours or overnight, until the batter smells pleasantly sour and has small bubbles on top.
Pour off any gray liquid from the surface and stir in the salt.
Whisk in up to [[0.5 cup]] more water if the batter feels thick, so it flows easily from a spoon.
Heat a large nonstick pan over medium heat with no oil.
Pour in a ladle of batter and swirl to make a thin round. Cover with a lid.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes, until the surface is covered with tiny holes and the top is dry. Do not flip it.
Slide onto a towel and let it cool in a single layer, then repeat with the remaining batter.

ing: or cayenne with a little cardamom
st: Steam or boil the collard greens with a pinch of salt for 10 minutes until tender. Drain, squeeze dry and chop.
Warm the niter kibbeh gently in a pan until melted, then take it off the heat.
Stir the mitmita and cardamom into the warm butter for 30 seconds.
Add the ground beef and stir for a few seconds. Traditional kitfo is served raw, but for safety cook it to 160°F (71°C), about 3 minutes in the pan, stirring.
For a lighter version, warm it only until the outside turns gray while the center stays red. Use only very fresh meat from a trusted butcher.
Season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and optional lemon juice.
Serve on a plate with the cheese and greens alongside and injera for scooping.
Cook the onion in a dry pot over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add [[3 tbsp]] oil, the garlic and [[1 tbsp]] berbere and cook 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until jammy.
Pour in [[2 cups]] water and bring to a simmer.
Whisk the chickpea flour into [[1 cup]] cold water until smooth.
Slowly pour the flour mixture into the pot, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Add [[1 tsp]] salt, lower the heat, and cook 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and silky.
Thin with a splash of water if needed and serve hot with injera.
Pat the meat dry and season with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Heat a large skillet over high heat until very hot, and add [[1.5 tbsp]] niter kibbeh.
Add half the meat in one layer and sear for 3 minutes without moving. Turn and sear 2 more minutes. Remove and repeat with the rest.
Lower the heat to medium and melt the remaining [[1.5 tbsp]] niter kibbeh in the same pan.
Add the onions and cook 4 minutes until soft and lightly browned.
Add the garlic, chili, rosemary and berbere and stir for 1 minute.
Return the meat and any juices and toss for 2 minutes to heat through. Beef should be at least 145°F (63°C).
Serve hot with injera or bread.
Cook the onions in a dry pot over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the niter kibbeh, garlic and ginger and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] berbere and the tomato and cook 5 minutes until thick.
Add the lentils and [[4 cups]] water and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer, stirring often, for 25 minutes until the lentils are completely soft and the stew is thick.
Add [[1 tsp]] salt and add a splash of water if the stew becomes too thick.
Spoon the warm lentils onto injera and serve with other stews.
Wash the collards well and chop them into thin ribbons.
Boil them in salted water for 10 minutes, then drain well.
Melt the niter kibbeh in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.
Add the collards, chili, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 cup]] water.
Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until very tender.
Uncover and cook 3 more minutes to cook off extra liquid, then serve.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
Add the carrots and potatoes along with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.75 cup]] water.
Cover and cook on medium-low for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage on top, cover, and cook another 20 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Stir gently, uncover, and cook 3 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Taste, adjust salt, and serve warm with injera.

ing: torn into small pieces, day-old is fine
st: Cook the onion in a dry pan over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the niter kibbeh and garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] berbere and cook 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.75 cup]] water, then simmer 8 minutes until thick.
Fold in the torn injera and toss until all pieces are coated.
Cook 2 more minutes so the injera softens and warms through.
Serve right away from the pan, ideally for breakfast.
Bring [[3.5 cups]] water and the salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Sprinkle in the barley flour slowly, then lower the heat.
Cook for 3 minutes without stirring so a skin forms.
Stir hard with a wooden spoon for 5 minutes until the porridge is smooth and stiff.
Cook another 5 minutes over low heat, stirring, until it no longer tastes raw.
Mound the porridge on a plate and press a hollow into the center.
Mix the melted niter kibbeh with the berbere and pour it into the hollow.
Serve with yogurt on the side, dipping each spoonful into the spiced butter.

ing: dried chili flakes or ground chili
st: Toast the fenugreek, cardamom, cumin, peppercorns and cloves in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Cool the toasted spices for 5 minutes.
Grind them to a fine powder in a spice grinder.
Mix the ground spices with the chili, paprika, ginger, garlic powder and salt in a bowl.
Stir well until the color is even.
Store in a jar in a cool dark place for up to 3 months.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over low heat.
Bring to a gentle simmer until foam forms on top, about 10 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic, ginger, cardamom, fenugreek, turmeric and cinnamon.
Simmer on very low heat for 30 to 40 minutes, skimming foam, until the milk solids sink and the butter is clear and fragrant.
Do not let the solids brown or burn.
Strain through a fine sieve lined with cheesecloth into a clean jar.
Cool and keep refrigerated for up to 3 months.
